chapter_name: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: Civil Disobedience and Beyond
learning_objective: 🕊️ Understand the charismatic leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, his methods of Satyagraha, and how he transformed the Indian freedom struggle into a true mass movement!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: सत्याग्रह (Soul force or truth force; non-violent resistance)
चरखा (Spinning wheel, symbol of self-reliance and nationalism)
असहयोग (Refusal to cooperate with the British government and institutions)
सविनय अवज्ञा (Peaceful, deliberate breaking of unjust laws)
हरिजन (Children of God; term coined by Gandhi for the 'untouchables')

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Returning from South Africa in 1915, Gandhi first intervened in local struggles in Champaran, Kheda, and Ahmedabad. By dressing in a simple dhoti and speaking the language of the masses, he deeply connected with the common Indian.

Following the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre, Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement. He joined hands with the Khilafat movement to foster Hindu-Muslim unity. It was called off abruptly after the violent Chauri Chaura incident.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🧂 The Salt March and Civil Disobedience (1930)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: To break the British monopoly on salt (an essential item for everyone), Gandhi marched from Sabarmati to Dandi and made salt from seawater. This launched the Civil Disobedience Movement, bringing global attention to India's struggle.

After the failure of the Cripps Mission, Gandhi launched his most militant mass movement, asking the British to 'Quit India'. Though most leaders were jailed immediately, young activists ran a massive underground resistance.

How do historians reconstruct Gandhi's life? They use a variety of sources: public speeches, private letters, autobiographies, highly biased police/intelligence reports, and both Indian and foreign newspaper clippings.

fun_activity.title: 🧂 The Power of a Pinch of Salt
fun_activity.instructions: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the symbol of protest? Because salt was consumed by everyone—rich or poor, Hindu or Muslim. The British heavily taxed this free gift of nature. By simply picking up a handful of salt, Gandhi instantly united 300 million Indians!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Non-Cooperation (refusing to help the government) and Civil Disobedience (actively breaking the law).
📌 Gandhi's speech at the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in 1916 is a major exam topic—he heavily criticized the elite for ignoring the poor peasants.
📌 Be prepared for an 8-mark question on the sources used to reconstruct the history of the national movement (letters, newspapers, police records).
quick_recap: ⭐ Gopal Krishna Gokhale was Mahatma Gandhi's acknowledged political mentor.
⭐ The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931 temporarily halted Civil Disobedience, leading Gandhi to attend the Second Round Table Conference in London.
⭐ On Independence Day (August 15, 1947), Gandhi was not celebrating in Delhi; he was in Noakhali (Bengal) trying to stop communal riots.
